subject.title: fix(qqbot): queued and in-flight messages are lost when the gateway resumes after reconnect or restart

question: Should a QQ Bot handler failure remain a terminal logged drop, or should it block the connection-wide RESUME cursor and require globally ordered retry before later events proceed?
rationale: The current patch chooses global replay without stopping later processing, which can turn one poison message into repeated duplicate delivery for unrelated later traffic; the permanent failure contract needs an explicit owner choice.

options.title: Preserve terminal failure semantics
options.body: Settle a message after its handler error is logged, while retaining delayed settlement for genuinely queued or in-flight messages interrupted by reconnect or restart.

options.title: Enforce globally ordered retry
options.body: Stop processing later gateway sequences after a failure until the failed event is successfully replayed, with cross-peer ordering and reconnect coverage.

options.title: Accept replay amplification
options.body: Land the current behavior knowing one persistent handler failure can replay all later connection-wide events on subsequent reconnects.

recommendation.title: Preserve terminal failure semantics
recommendation.body: Settle a message after its handler error is logged, while retaining delayed settlement for genuinely queued or in-flight messages interrupted by reconnect or restart.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision changes the failure and ordering contract of the QQ Bot gateway and queue architecture they introduced.
